project.title: Human control-to-company transaction fence
project.goal: Order SQLite revocation against authorized company commit
project.scope: Internal admitted-connection R04/R13 increment; no live/product writer authority

action.control_fence.description: Authorize current human control facts while holding control writer lock across company commit

errors.fence_refused: Refuse before callback/commit; checked rollback and reuse status.
errors.outcome_unknown: Retire connections and recover commit outcome; do not claim rollback.

preconditions: Trusted authenticated human/provider observation, stable distinct admitted databases, manifest/lifetime fencing and trusted synchronous callback.
postconditions: Known company commit plus control reuse status, or typed precommit/unknown failure. No deliberate control changes.

authorization.rationale: Protect control observation through company commit; preserve known commit and unknown outcomes; external authentication/manifest admission remain explicit preconditions.

boundaries.rationale: Protect control observation through company commit; preserve known commit and unknown outcomes; external authentication/manifest admission remain explicit preconditions.

atomicity.rationale: Protect control observation through company commit; preserve known commit and unknown outcomes; external authentication/manifest admission remain explicit preconditions.

concurrency.rationale: Protect control observation through company commit; preserve known commit and unknown outcomes; external authentication/manifest admission remain explicit preconditions.

idempotency.rationale: Protect control observation through company commit; preserve known commit and unknown outcomes; external authentication/manifest admission remain explicit preconditions.

action.control_fence.behavior: Control immediate lock, strict current admission, actual rows, shared policy, company immediate transaction, explicit outcome and release

boundary.responsibility: Current control authorization and SQLite transaction orchestration
boundary.rationale: Actual commits require ordered current control facts.
excludes: Provider verification, stable path/lifetime admission, manifest locking, domain posting and product endpoints

scenario.normal.description: Actual current control rows allow exactly one authorized company commit and no control data changes.

scenario.given: Canonical synthetic control DB and isolated transaction-effect ledger.
scenario.when: Execute native fenced transaction or synchronized independent revoker/crash child.
scenario.then: Actual current control rows allow exactly one authorized company commit and no control data changes.

scenario.refusal.description: Missing session/current access, wrong scope/permission or invalid connection/source admission refuse before callback.

scenario.given: Canonical synthetic control DB and isolated transaction-effect ledger.
scenario.when: Execute native fenced transaction or synchronized independent revoker/crash child.
scenario.then: Missing session/current access, wrong scope/permission or invalid connection/source admission refuse before callback.

scenario.preservation.description: Business/SQL errors roll back sequence and companion effects; prior control state survives.

scenario.given: Canonical synthetic control DB and isolated transaction-effect ledger.
scenario.when: Execute native fenced transaction or synchronized independent revoker/crash child.
scenario.then: Business/SQL errors roll back sequence and companion effects; prior control state survives.

scenario.correction.description: Postcommit cleanup failure preserves success; commit/manual transaction escape reports unknown rather than false rollback.

scenario.given: Canonical synthetic control DB and isolated transaction-effect ledger.
scenario.when: Execute native fenced transaction or synchronized independent revoker/crash child.
scenario.then: Postcommit cleanup failure preserves success; commit/manual transaction escape reports unknown rather than false rollback.

scenario.concurrent.description: Separate processes serialize revoke/post; kill before commit rolls back and kill after commit preserves effects and releases locks.
